clues.clue: This Windows 11 edition is required to join an Active Directory domain.
clues.explain: Windows 11 Home cannot join an Active Directory domain; Windows 11 Pro adds domain join, Group Policy management, and BitLocker, making it the entry-level business edition.

clues.clue: This Windows 10 edition supports BitLocker full-volume encryption.
clues.explain: BitLocker full-volume encryption is available on Windows 10 Pro and Enterprise; the Home edition does not include BitLocker, only Device Encryption in limited scenarios.

clues.clue: EFS (Encrypting File System) is exclusive to these two Windows editions, never available in Home.
clues.response: What are Windows Pro and Enterprise?
clues.explain: EFS per-file encryption is available only in Pro and Enterprise editions; Home editions are explicitly excluded, so sensitive per-file encryption requires an upgrade.

clues.clue: When a TPM chip is not present, BitLocker can store its startup key on this removable device instead.
clues.response: What is a USB flash drive?
clues.explain: Without a TPM, BitLocker can place the startup key on a USB flash drive that must be inserted at boot; the drive acts as a physical token replacing the TPM's sealed-key function.

clues.clue: This deprecated Windows group, kept only for legacy app compatibility, had its elevated rights removed starting with Windows Vista.
clues.response: What is the Power Users Group?
clues.explain: Beginning with Windows Vista, the Power Users group was stripped of its XP-era elevated permissions and retained solely so older software that checks for group membership does not break.

clues.clue: In a Windows command prompt, this command with two dots moves you up one directory level.
clues.explain: cd .. (change directory followed by double-dot) navigates up one level in the folder hierarchy; chaining it as cd ..\..\ moves up multiple levels in one step.

clues.clue: Before running sfc, you run this DISM command to repair the component store so sfc has valid source files to restore from.
clues.explain: If Windows Update's component store is corrupt, sfc cannot restore files correctly; DISM /RestoreHealth pulls clean binaries from Microsoft and repairs the store first.

clues.clue: This chkdsk switch fixes file-system errors without scanning for bad sectors, and can often run without a reboot on non-system volumes.
clues.explain: chkdsk /f fixes logical file-system errors (lost clusters, cross-links); unlike /r it skips the physical bad-sector scan, so it can run on a mounted data volume without rebooting.

clues.clue: Within diskpart, this single command removes all partition and volume information from the selected disk.
clues.explain: The diskpart 'clean' command zeroes the MBR and partition table (or GPT header) of the selected disk, removing all partition and volume information so the disk appears unallocated.

clues.clue: This dir switch sorts the listing by file extension, useful when scanning a directory for all files of a given type.
clues.explain: dir /OE (Order by Extension) sorts directory output alphabetically by file extension, making it straightforward to spot groups of .txt, .log, or .exe files without piping through findstr.

clues.clue: This Windows feature pops up a dialog asking what to do when you insert a USB drive or optical disc; setting it to 'Take no action' hardens a system against malicious media.
clues.explain: AutoPlay prompts the user to pick an action (open folder, play, import) when media is inserted -- unlike AutoRun, which silently executes code via autorun.inf. Setting AutoPlay to 'Take no action' is the hardening step.

clues.clue: This password policy setting forces users to wait a defined duration before they can attempt to log in again after too many failed tries.
clues.response: What is the Account Lockout Duration?
clues.explain: Account Lockout Duration sets how many minutes a locked account remains inaccessible; combined with the lockout threshold it slows brute-force attacks by imposing mandatory waiting periods.

clues.clue: A smart card used with a PIN is an example of MFA because it combines these two authentication factor categories.
clues.response: What are something you have and something you know?
clues.explain: A smart card is 'something you have' (a physical token); the PIN is 'something you know'; together they satisfy two distinct MFA factor categories, which is the definition of multi-factor authentication.

clues.clue: To recover EFS-encrypted files after a user account is deleted, a technician uses this previously exported item.
clues.response: What is the EFS recovery agent certificate (or Data Recovery Agent certificate)?
clues.explain: A Data Recovery Agent (DRA) certificate, exported before the account was lost, lets an administrator decrypt EFS files whose original user keys are gone; without it the data is unrecoverable.

clues.clue: This technique can bypass MAC filtering because wireless NICs allow their hardware address to be changed in software.
clues.explain: MAC addresses can be changed at the software level on most NICs; an attacker sniffs a permitted MAC from wireless traffic and then spoofs it, defeating MAC filtering as a sole access control.

clues.clue: This command-line utility can also force-terminate a non-responding process by name when Task Manager itself is unavailable.
clues.explain: taskkill /F /IM processname.exe forcefully terminates a process by image name from the command prompt; it is useful when the GUI Task Manager cannot be launched or is itself hung.

clues.clue: This boot environment, accessible from Advanced Startup Options, lets a technician restore the OS to a prior snapshot without booting into Windows normally.
clues.response: What is System Restore (from the Recovery Environment)?
clues.explain: The Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) includes System Restore, allowing a technician to roll back system files and registry to a restore point even when the OS will not boot.

clues.clue: If an app crashes in both Safe Mode AND normal mode, this is identified as the likely source of the problem.
clues.response: What is the application itself (or a corrupted application file)?
clues.explain: Safe Mode loads only essential drivers; if the crash persists there, the third-party driver set is eliminated as the cause, pointing to the application's own files or a corrupt installation.

clues.clue: A phone's battery drains abnormally fast within two hours of a full charge; do this before replacing the battery.
clues.response: What is check and disable background apps or sync services consuming power?
clues.explain: Background processes, push email, and location services are common causes of rapid battery drain; disabling them is the first diagnostic step to confirm the battery hardware is actually at fault.

clues.clue: This PowerShell cmdlet launches Microsoft Defender's offline scan, rebooting the PC into the Windows Recovery Environment to remove rootkits before Windows loads.
clues.explain: Start-MpWDOScan triggers Microsoft Defender Offline: the PC reboots into WinRE and scans before Windows starts, catching persistent rootkits that hide once the OS (even Safe Mode) is running.

clues.clue: MBR partitioning supports a maximum of this many primary partitions on a single disk.
clues.explain: An MBR partition table holds a maximum of four primary partitions; to create more, one primary partition must be converted to an extended partition containing logical drives.

clues.clue: This NTFS feature records changes to the file system in a log before completing them, allowing recovery after a power failure.
clues.explain: NTFS uses a transaction log (journal) to record pending changes; if a write is interrupted, Windows replays or rolls back the journal on reboot, preventing file-system corruption.

clues.clue: GPT uses this type of globally unique identifier to label each partition, distinguishing it from MBR's simple numeric scheme.
clues.response: What is a GUID (Globally Unique Identifier)?
clues.explain: GPT assigns each partition a 128-bit GUID, which is where the partition table format gets its name; this scheme supports up to 128 partitions on Windows without the MBR primary-partition limit.

clues.clue: Windows sends this command to an SSD during its weekly optimization pass, marking deleted blocks so the drive can erase them efficiently.
clues.explain: TRIM (ATA Data Set Management command) tells an SSD which logical block addresses are no longer in use, allowing the controller to erase those cells proactively and maintain write performance.

clues.clue: In Windows Disk Management, this type of volume spans multiple physical disks to appear as one large drive letter.
clues.explain: A spanned volume (also called JBOD -- Just a Bunch of Disks) combines free space from two or more physical disks into a single drive letter; it offers no redundancy, so one disk failure loses all data.

clues.clue: This short-range wireless standard, operating at 13.56 MHz, is also used to read contactless smart cards for building access control.
clues.explain: NFC at 13.56 MHz is the same radio standard used by contactless smart-card access systems (such as ISO 14443 cards); phones with NFC can emulate these cards for logical or physical access.

clues.clue: This tethering method connects a single PC to a phone's cellular data using only a USB cable, requiring no Wi-Fi radio.
clues.explain: USB tethering shares the phone's cellular connection over the USB cable as a virtual network adapter; it also charges the phone and avoids interference or security risks of wireless hotspot mode.

clues.clue: After replacing a cracked screen, a user reports that touch input registers a few centimeters away from where they tap; this calibration issue is resolved by doing this.
clues.response: What is recalibrating the touchscreen (or running the digitizer calibration utility)?
clues.explain: A replacement digitizer may not be perfectly aligned with the display; running the OS touch-calibration routine teaches the device to map raw digitizer coordinates to correct screen positions.

clues.clue: Before a factory reset, this account credential must be known or removed from the device to prevent activation lock from making the device unusable afterward.
clues.response: What is the Google account (or Apple ID)?
clues.explain: Android Factory Reset Protection and Apple Activation Lock tie the device to the signed-in account; if the credential is unknown and not removed before the reset, the device is locked post-wipe.

clues.clue: Unlike TACACS+, this AAA protocol encrypts only the password field in its packets and combines authentication and authorization into a single process.
clues.explain: RADIUS encrypts only the password field (not the full payload) and merges authentication with authorization in one exchange; TACACS+ was designed to address both weaknesses by encrypting everything and separating the three AAA functions.
